entries.name: partial information decomposition
entries.senseHere: A method that splits what several input neurons tell you about one target neuron into shared, unique, and combined-only parts.
entries.background: Proposed by Williams and Beer in 2010 as a way to break Shannon's information measures into finer pieces.

entries.name: rich club
entries.senseHere: A set of the best-connected neurons that are linked to one another more densely than chance would predict. In these recordings they carry most of the information traffic.

entries.name: multielectrode array
entries.background: A grid of tiny electrodes that records the electrical firing of many neurons at the same time.

entries.name: mutual information
entries.senseHere: A measure of how much knowing one neuron's activity reduces uncertainty about another's, regardless of direction or timing.

entries.name: transfer entropy
entries.senseHere: A measure of how much one neuron's past activity helps predict another's next activity, beyond what the second neuron's own past already predicts.

entries.name: functional connectivity
entries.senseHere: A measure of how similar or statistically linked the activity of two neurons is, without any sense of direction.

entries.name: effective connectivity
entries.senseHere: A map of which neurons influence which others, with direction, inferred from how their activity unfolds over time.

entries.name: synergy
entries.senseHere: Information about a target neuron that appears only when two or more input neurons are considered together, and not from either one alone.

entries.name: redundancy
entries.senseHere: Information about the target neuron that is carried identically by more than one input neuron, so it gets counted twice if you add them up.

entries.name: unique information
entries.senseHere: Information about the target neuron that only one particular input neuron provides and the other does not.

entries.name: redundancy function
entries.senseHere: A formula chosen to say how much information several sources share. PID needs one to work, and researchers have not agreed on a single best one.

entries.name: computational triad
entries.senseHere: A group of three neurons in which two source neurons both send connections to a common target neuron. Each such group is analyzed separately.

entries.name: partial information lattice
entries.senseHere: An ordered diagram of all the distinct ways a group of sources can share, or uniquely hold, information about a target. Each node is one such 'atom'.

entries.name: Möbius inversion
entries.background: A mathematical technique for recovering the individual contributions of each level of an ordered structure from cumulative totals.

entries.name: organotypic cultures
entries.background: Thin slices of brain tissue kept alive in nutrient fluid so their cells keep much of their natural wiring.

entries.name: DIT
entries.background: A Python software package offering many information-theory measures, including many PID redundancy functions.

entries.name: IDTxl
entries.background: A Python software package for information-theoretic analysis of time series, including transfer entropy and PID tools.

entries.name: Dedekind number
entries.background: A sequence counting certain collections of subsets that grows astonishingly fast. Only the first several terms are known.

entries.name: O-information
entries.background: A single number that tells whether a group of variables is dominated by shared (redundant) or combined-only (synergistic) information.

entries.name: local PID
entries.senseHere: A version of PID that works out the information parts for each individual moment in time, rather than averaging over a whole recording.

entries.name: neuronal avalanches
entries.background: Cascades of neural firing that spread through a network, with sizes following a particular pattern often linked to systems poised at a critical point.

entries.name: integrated information decomposition
entries.senseHere: An extension of PID that handles several targets at once, for example splitting how the past of a system shares information with its future.
